body.p: Applicant has reviewed the Office action dated December 6, 2021, and the references cited therein. Claims 1-13 are currently pending and stand rejected. Claims 14-15 have been canceled. Claim 16 is withdrawn from consideration. Applicant's Amendments to the Claims

Applicant, in accordance with the original disclosure, has amended the claims to more particularly specify the locations of the electrodes with respect to the wearer's torso "near the thoracic diaphragm." Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the grounds for rejection of the

previously pending claims in view of Applicant's further amendments to the claims and remarks addressing the shortcomings of the prior art with regard to particular recited elements of the claimed invention.
Please charge any fee deficiencies to Deposit Account No. 12-1216. Grounds for Rejecting the Claims
1. Claims 1-5 and 11 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Berg, U.S. Pub. No. 2015/0148619 (Berg).
2. Claim 6 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Berg in view of McGrane, U.S. Pub. No. 2017/0019988 (McGrane).
3. Claim 7 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Berg in view of Maesani, U.S. Pub. No. 2017/0273590 (Maesani).
4. Claims 8 and 10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Berg in view of Maesani as applied to claim 7, and in further view of Muccio, U.S. Pub No. 2012/0016440 (Muccio).
5. Claim 9 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Berg in view of Hsiao, U.S. Pub. No. 2012/0265025 (Hsiao).
6. Claim 12 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Berg as applied to claim 1, and further in view of Sims, U.S. Pub. No. 2007/0293781 (Sims).
7. Claim 13 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Berg as applied to claim 1, and further in view of Tupin, U.S. Pub. No. 2011/0060215 (Tupin).
Applicant traverses the grounds for each and every rejection for at least the reasons set forth herein below. Applicant addresses the specific rejections in the order they arise in the Office Action.
Applicant's Specific Responses to the Grounds for Rejection
1. Rejection of Claims 1-5 and 11 as anticipated by Berg

Applicant traverses the rejection of claims 1-5 and 11, as being anticipated by the teachings of Berg. Berg does not anticipate any of the currently pending claims since the teachings of the cited Berg reference do not describe each recited element of any currently pending claim for at least the reasons stated herein below.

Moreover, a proper reason cannot be established, based upon the teachings of Berg, for one skilled in the art to modify Berg's teachings, in a way that would result in Applicant's claimed invention. Notably, none of the references demonstrates any awareness of a particularized problem that would provide a reason to modify Berg in a way that resulted in Applicants' claimed invention.
a. Applicant's Claimed Invention
Applicant's claimed invention is directed to a wearable device including a particular

electrode arrangement that facilitates monitoring vital signs (i.e., carrying out electromyography of the thoracic diaphragm) of its wearer. In particular claim 1, provided in clean form below, recites:
A wearable device for monitoring one or more vital signs of a human
body, the wearable device comprising:
a carrier configured to fit, while in use, fully around the human body, at an
abdominal part thereof; and
an electrode arrangement comprising a plurality of conductive electrodes,

wherein the electrodes are arranged on the carrier to be brought in contact with a skin of the body in use, and wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes are configured for operating simultaneously to receive electric physiologic signals from the body for enabling monitoring of a membrane potential of one or more
muscles in the body,
wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes arranged on the carrier

comprise one or more first electrodes arranged on the carrier to be in contact with a side part of a torso of the body near the thoracic diaphragm, said first electrodes being configured to cooperatively receive a first electrical signal
indicative of a membrane potential of a thoracic diaphragm of the body;
wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes arranged on the carrier

further comprises at least one second electrode in addition to the one or more first electrodes, the at least one second electrode being arranged on the carrier to be in contact with a mid front part of the abdominal part of the body simultaneously

with the first electrodes that receive the first electric signal indicative of said membrane potential of the thoracic diaphragm of the body, and to be aligned with the one or more first electrodes, the at least one second electrode thereby being arranged for receiving a second electrical signal indicative of one or more further electric physiologic signals from the body, for enabling filtering of the first electrical signal using the second electrical signal for enabling electromyography
of the thoracic diaphragm. (Emphasis added).

Thus, Applicant's claimed invention provides a particular arrangement, including first electrodes and second electrodes for monitoring activity of the thoracic diaphragm. Applicant's currently clarified claimed invention defines a configuration of the first/second electrodes for particularly monitoring activity of the thoracic diaphragm. In that regard, the claimed invention recites placing the electrodes at positions to specifically enable acquiring signals indicating the activity of the thoracic diaphragm, which are relatively weaker (and thus more difficult to sense) than a cardiac signal. See Applicant's specification at page 3, lines 13-14. Furthermore, as shown in Applicant's FIG. 2a (included below), the thoracic diaphragm (element 16) has a curved shape. Applicant's claimed second electrode provides an additional signal that is taken from the mid front part of the body. The signal provided by the second electrode includes distortions as well as the relatively/comparatively strong cardiac signal, but does not include the thoracic diaphragm signal that, due to the curved shape of the wearer's diaphragm, is much weaker or absent in the area where the second electrode's signal is acquired. See Applicant's specification at page 4, lines 3-19. In this regard, Applicant's FIGs. 2a, 2b and 2c are reproduced below that illustratively depict placement of the carrier (and first/second electrodes) on a pre-term baby to facilitate acquiring signals via the first and second electrodes in accordance with Applicant's claimed invention.

FIG. 2a depicts the curved shape of the thoracic diaphragm 16. See Applicant's specification at page 12, lines 2-5. Applicant's FIGs. 2b and 2c illustratively depict positioning of the belt with respect to the baby's front side and back side. The location of electrode 20 on the mid front side (per FIG. 2b) is advantageous over the back side - in view of the presence of the spine which diminishes the filter signal. See Applicant's specification at page 12, lines 6-12. Applicant's claimed invention is directed to a combination of first and second electrodes, and placement of specific ones of these two distinct electrodes, at specifically recited areas of the wearer, that facilitates obtaining: (1) a raw signal containing the thoracic diaphragm signal (as well as other non-thoracic diaphragm signals), and (2) a signal that facilitates filtering non-diaphragm signals to from the raw signal to obtain the thoracic diaphragm signal.
b. The Cited Berg Reference does not anticipate Applicant's claimed invention

Applicant, in view of the current clarifying amendment to independent claim 1, traverses the rejection of independent claim 1 over the teachings of Berg. Berg, upon which the rejection of claim 1 solely relies, describes (in FIG. 3B specifically) a shirt including sensors placed on a t-shirt to take measurements on the upper torso of a wearer. The Office action, at page 4, states:
"Fig 3b shows a second electrode(s) that are in contact with the mid front part of
the abdomen. Based on the claim language, the Examiner is interpreting this
claim to mean that one electrode can measure one electrical signal and the other
can measure another electrical signal. In light of this. Par. 0031 discloses EMG
electrodes that can measure different electrical signals"

An annotated/edited version of Berg's FIG. 3B is provided b, wherein the added dashed lines indicate the areas to the side where (per Applicant's now-clarified claim 1) the thoracic diaphragm signal can be sensed, and the mid front part wherein a filter signal is obtainable.

Berg does, indeed, relate to electromyography (EMG) for exercise tracking. See Berg, at paragraph [0003]. More particularly, Berg relates to "monitoring biometric signals of a user comprising: a garment", "a set of biometric sensors" and "a portable control module". See Berg, claim 1. Berg's very general description of EMG, coupled with the positioning of sensors on an upper torso location of a t-shirt, neither describes or even remotely suggests carrying out EMG with respect to a wearer's thoracic diaphragm. Berg does not describe/discuss measuring an EMG of the diaphragm, nor does Berg describe a particular layout and combination of signals that may be used to perform EMG of a wearer's thoracic diaphragm. Berg mentions measuring thoracic activity. However, given the placement of the sensors in FIG. 3B, Berg is merely generally describing acquiring EMG signals (from sensors placed at the upper torso). Berg does not describe acquiring an EMG signal that measures activity of the thoracic diaphragm.
Moreover, Berg does not describe/suggest obtaining a filter signal from a different part of the wearer's body that enables measuring a specific signal, by filtering out other signals using the

filter signal. In particular, Berg does not describe/suggest the above-mentioned combination of electrodes/signals in the particular acquisition locations to provide a thoracic diaphragm signal from a raw sensor signal and a second (filtering) signal that facilitates rendering a filtered signal containing the thoracic diaphragm signal. In that regard, Berg is silent with regard to positioning the sensors on the torso in a way that enables providing an EMG signal of the thoracic diaphragm.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant's currently amended independent claim 1 is not anticipated by Berg.
c. The dependent claims are not rendered obvious by the cited reference's teaching

Applicant traverses the rejection of dependent claims 2-5 and 11 for at least the reasons discussed above with reference to claim 1.

Applicant reserves the right to provide additional reasons for distinguishing claims 2-5 and 11 from the teachings of the prior art in the event that any further Office action recites new grounds for rejecting claims 2-5 and 11, or any claim from which claims 2-5 and 11 depend.
